muskogee-residents-bused-workers-to-smit.core: Posted in last 7 days Muskogee Residents - Bused Workers To Smith Ferry Road Facilities QUESTIONS RAISED ABOUT WORKERS BEING BUSED INTO MUSKOGEE INDUSTRIAL FACILITIES Social media posts are raising questions about buses transporting workers to industrial facilities along Smith Ferry Road in Muskogee, Oklahoma. In several posts on X, @ShaBacksTheBlue (County MAGA) alleges that approximately five buses are transporting undocumented immigrants to newly developed industrial facilities. The account claims these workers are taking local jobs and housing and has tagged DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin in the posts. But what do we actually know? The Smith Ferry Road area has experienced significant industrial development, including Google’s massive Project Scissortail data center campus. Nearby, Stardust Power is developing a battery-grade lithium refinery, with hundreds of projected jobs. Meanwhile, Village Travel, a regional charter bus company, has advertised employee shuttle driver positions in Muskogee. The listings describe transporting workers to local plants and factories for first, second, and third shifts, with drivers earning approximately $220 or more per day. These listings are consistent with reports of employee shuttle activity, although the specific routes and employers have not been independently established. What remains unverified is the allegation that the passengers are undocumented immigrants. No identified reports from local news organizations, ICE, DHS, or Muskogee officials have confirmed those claims. The circulating social media posts have not provided independent evidence establishing the workers’ immigration status. Oklahoma manufacturers have experienced labor shortages, and some employers statewide have utilized legal temporary foreign worker programs. However, no connection between those programs and these particular shuttle operations has been established. There are legitimate questions worth investigating: Who is contracting these buses? Which companies employ the passengers? Are staffing agencies involved? Are any foreign worker programs being utilized? The industrial development and employee shuttle job advertisements are documented. The immigration allegations remain unsubstantiated. If you live in the Muskogee area and have firsthand information about these buses or the companies involved, I’d like to hear from you. #Muskogee #OklahomaNews #Immigration #SmithFerryRoad #InvestigativeReporting

survivors-of-sexual-exploitation-parenta.author: Priscilla Iwedike
survivors-of-sexual-exploitation-parenta.core: Posted in last 7 days Survivors of Sexual Exploitation - Parental Blame & Stigma I had a conversation while working on a story recently, and honestly, something the survivor said has stayed with me. I didn't know she was a survivor of sexual exploitation until we started talking. She eventually opened up but requested anonymity, which I respected. What struck me most was how she described her relationship with her parents. She said they made her feel like a failure. Imagine experiencing sexual abuse and still being afraid to tell your parents because you fear being blamed rather than protected. Think about that. A child would rather carry such trauma alone than risk confiding in the people who are supposed to be her safe place. And this brings me to something we don't discuss enough: the damage some parents do with their words. Why have we normalised making children feel like failures because they haven't achieved what their mates have? I recently watched a video of a young man threatening to sell his mother during an argument involving comparisons with people online. I also saw a video of a young lady recording her parent's repeated insults towards her. Must we wait until a child is pushed into depression or even suicide before we start blaming the devil or village people? Not every battle is spiritual. Sometimes, the pain a child is carrying comes from the very people who are supposed to love and protect them. Parents, your children are not your competition. They are not failures because their journey looks different. And when a child speaks up about sexual abuse, believe them, listen to them and protect them. They don't need another person to blame them. I recently reported on this survivor's experience for The Guardian, Nigeria .It is an important conversation we need to have as a society, and I invite you to read the full report: https://lnkd.in/e_82KAy5 I want to hear your thoughts. Have some parents become so consumed by comparison and expectations that they have forgotten how to make their children feel safe? And if you are a survivor willing to share your experience, including anonymously, you can reach out to me. Your story deserves to be heard, and your identity respected. Let's talk about it. I remain Priscilla Iwedike- your unwavering voice, reporting the truth in every line #Parenting #ChildProtection #SexualAbuseAwareness #MentalHealthAwareness #EndChildAbuse #SurvivorVoices #TheGuardian #SocialResponsibility The Guardian Nigeria

nigerian-ethnic-group-members-share-cult.author: Eyitemi Asagba
nigerian-ethnic-group-members-share-cult.core: Posted in last 7 days Nigerian Ethnic Group Members - Share Culture, Photos & Histories A Journey Through Nigeria’s Cultural Heritage As we begin this cultural exploration with Beyond Dates, I want to start with a people I proudly call my own. The main source of the account of the origin of the Urhobo people is oral tradition. According to Onigu Otite, the Urhobo tradition can be broken down into four accounts or theories. Oral traditions among some of the Urhobo assert that Urhobo did not migrate from anywhere before settling in their present location. Another account of origin of the Urhobo people has of that they migrated from Benin particularly during the Ogiso and Egbeka dynasty. It should be noted however, that it is not all the clans that are unanimous on this account of origin. For example, while Olomu, Agbon and Abram’s clans claim to have migrated from Benin, others such as Ughelli and Ewu clans believe they have come from the Ijo-speaking people of Delta state. The third historical account of the traditional origin of the Urhobo holds the view that the Urhobo migrated from Ile-Ife territory in the western part of Nigeria. This belief is based on the view that there is a large concentration of Urhobo in and around Ile-Ife today. And lastly, is the more tenuous tradition which holds that the earliest inhabitants of the Urhobo territory migrated from Sudan and Egypt like the Yoruba and Edo speaking people. Now, I will get a little personal. My name is Ogheneovo, which means “God is one”. I come from Sapele, and its historical roots are particularly associated with the Okpe Urhobo people. Sapele lies along the Ethiope river, which historically provided access for trade and movement between inland communities and the coast. I think food deserves a particularly colorful part of this series. Urhobo cuisine offers a lot of variety, especially because of its relationship between the people and their Niger Delta environment. Of course, my favorite is starch and banga soup (Usi and Amiedi). Urhobo political history is particularly interesting because it was not historically organized under one centralized monarch. Instead, Urhobo society developed through different autonomous communities and clans. A traditional ruler in several Urhobo kingdoms and communities is called “Ovie”. We also have the roles of “Orodje”, “Okakuro”, and “Otata” It is important not to assume that every Urhobo community uses the same titles, the Okpe political system, for example, has its own historical structure involving four groups associated with the sons of Okpe: Orhue, Evwreke, Orhoro and Esezi. Now that I have begun this series from a personal perspective, it is time to hear from you! Send me a message telling me your ethnic group and, if possible, the specific state you come from. Share photographs, or family histories. Don’t assume your culture is too small, too familiar or too obscure to be featured. Every community has a story, we want to hear yours! Let’s discover Nigeria, one people and one story at a time. 🇳🇬 Beyond Dates

anoka-county-and-monticello-witnesses-un.headline: Anoka County & Monticello Witnesses - Unidentified Lights Feb 2025
anoka-county-and-monticello-witnesses-un.author: 𝗖𝗥𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗔 𝗚𝗢𝗠𝗘𝗭
anoka-county-and-monticello-witnesses-un.core: Posted in last 7 days Anoka County & Monticello Witnesses - Unidentified Lights Feb 2025 At 1:17 a.m. on February 19, 2025, a small group of Anoka Police Department employees was wrapping up an after-action briefing in a Domino’s parking lot, just up the road from the station, then someone looked west. Low on the western horizon, over the Lake Minnetonka area, was a SPHERE OF LIGHT that would not hold one color. It kept flashing and shifting between red, blue, green and white. One witness compared it to a tie-dye shirt in motion. Another described six “hula-hoops with lights around each loop,” like the textbook drawing of an atom. They put it at the size of an SUV or a school bus, possibly 50 miles away, somewhere between 10,000 and 30,000 feet up. This was not a glimpse. They watched it for about 90 minutes, until the cold finally drove them inside. The group moved to the Anoka Municipal Ramp for a better view, and one officer got binoculars. In the witness’s FBI interview, a small private plane approached from the southeast. The object dropped, moved around the plane’s path, climbed back up and went back to hovering. The witness’s earlier report to Americans for Safe Aerospace adds a helicopter. When it flew between the witnesses and the object, the object shot north and gained altitude. One account says it covered 30 to 40 miles in seconds and “skipped across the sky like a stone.” The witness wrote that it moved like no aircraft or satellite he knew. Then it moved west in three separate bursts, toward Monticello, home of the Monticello Nuclear Generating Plant. It hovered, then came down “like a leaf floating on a breeze.” The ASA report opens by warning that the case might involve nuclear energy infrastructure. On his way to meet someone at a Kwik Trip, the witness says he spotted a second, similar object. He told the FBI he followed it 12 miles down Highway 10 and watched it hover over Monticello. A coworker also drove toward the first object, all the way to Elk River. It was still far to the west. It was not the first time either. Around 11:30 p.m. on February 17, two days earlier, the same officer was on patrol when he spotted a “diamond-shaped object” covered in multicolored lights. For about 10 minutes, he says, it moved in every direction at speeds he had never seen. Then it took off and disappeared. He told no one until his coworkers saw the second one with him. His FBI interview also mentions an object near the Anoka Ice Arena on September 11, 2022, that hovered and then climbed out of sight. He filmed that one on his phone. The public release has one clip. It is blurry and three seconds long, filmed by pointing an iPhone into a pair of binoculars. The officer himself called the footage “nearly useless and blurry.” It was too cold that night to use magnified optics or night vision. The files describe a second video, taken in daylight by another witness, that may show the object flying a long racetrack loop. That video is not attached. The tip reached the FBI through ASA, the nonprofit founded by former Navy pilot Ryan Graves. Graves says his team found the report credible. In May 2025, an FBI agent interviewed the witness in his office at the Anoka Police Department. The case was then closed without further investigative action. The files never identify the object, and they never explain it. Anoka Police Chief Andy Youngquist confirms at least one witness is a sworn officer. He says the department has had no new sightings reported since. Graves was careful about what that means. ASA documents these reports and pushes for safety. It does not say the objects are alien. I want to be straight with you here... A light that sits low on the horizon, changes color constantly and stays in roughly the same part of the sky for 90 minutes fits a very ordinary suspect: a bright star or planet. Near the horizon, the atmosphere makes them flash red, green, blue and white. An out-of-focus point of light in handheld binoculars
